prompts.topic_ko: 16:9 3칸 시트, 전신 칸 얼굴 가리기, 소품 시트
prompts.label: COPY AND CUSTOMIZE
prompts.subject: YOUR CHARACTER PROMPT
prompts.prompt:
[Describe your character: age, face, hairstyle, build, outfit and
shoes.]
Create a 16:9 character sheet with three equal-width panels in one horizontal
row on a flat neutral grey studio background. Use soft, even lighting,
balanced exposure and visible natural skin texture. No environment, props or
text labels. No hard shadows on the backdrop.
Panel 1: front-facing close-up of the head and shoulders, with clearly defined
facial features.
Panel 2: full body, front view, neutral standing pose, head and shoes fully
visible.
Panel 3: full body, back view, same standing pose and scale, head and shoes
fully visible.
Keep the same identity, hairstyle, body proportions, outfit, materials and
colors across all three panels.

prompts.topic_ko: 16:9 3칸 시트, 전신 칸 얼굴 가리기, 소품 시트
prompts.label: COPY INTO YOUR IMAGE EDITOR
prompts.subject: AFTER GENERATION: FACE EDIT
prompts.prompt:
Edit only the front full-body panel. Hide its facial features with a flat grey color
matching the backdrop. Preserve the hair, head outline, neck, body and clothes.
Leave the close-up portrait and back view unchanged.

prompts.topic_ko: 16:9 3칸 시트, 전신 칸 얼굴 가리기, 소품 시트
prompts.label: PROP SHEET PROMPT
prompts.subject: A SEPARATE SHEET FOR PROPS
prompts.prompt:
[Describe your prop: shape, material, color and distinctive details.]
Create a 16:9 two-panel prop sheet on a flat neutral grey studio background.
Use soft, even lighting. No environment or text labels. No hard shadows on the
backdrop.
Panel 1: front-facing close-up of the prop, showing its distinctive details.
Panel 2: full shot of the entire prop, fully inside the frame.
Keep the same shape, materials, colors and proportions in both panels.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Describe real skin instead of asking for hyper-realism
prompts.label: BETTER
prompts.subject: Describe real skin instead of asking for hyper-realism
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic close-up of a woman of about 30 sitting by a kitchen window on a gray morning, holding a mug of coffee and looking just past the camera with a half smile. Shot on an 85 mm lens at eye level, about a meter from her face. Soft daylight from the window on her left, the right side of her face falling into gentle shadow. Real, unretouched skin with faint freckles across her nose, a little shine on her forehead, fine lines at the corners of her eyes as she smiles and a few loose strands of hair across her cheek. No readable text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Describe real skin instead of asking for hyper-realism
prompts.label: REALISM BLOCK
prompts.subject: The realism block
prompts.prompt: Real, unretouched photographic skin: natural color variation across the face, a little shine on the forehead and nose, softer texture on the outer cheeks, normal creases under the eyes and real texture on the lips. Hair separates into uneven strands with a few flyaways, and makeup and clothing look lived in. A natural, in-the-moment expression rather than a posed model look. It reads as a frame from a film, not a stock photo or a beauty ad. No skin smoothing, waxy skin, porcelain teeth, glowing irises, uniform pore texture or helmet-like hair.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Use one light with a reason to be there
prompts.label: LIGHT BLOCK
prompts.subject: Use one light with a reason to be there
prompts.prompt: One [light source] [where it sits] lights [the person]'s face in [warm amber] light from [the left]. The rest of the [room] falls into deep [green-gray] shadow, [with a little haze in the beam]. No other light sources and no flat fill light.

prompts.section: Write a person, not a model
prompts.label: IMAGE PROMPT
prompts.subject: The detective
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic medium shot of a man of 62, a police detective, heavy-set and rumpled, with ruddy weathered skin, gray stubble, thinning gray hair combed back and tired bloodshot eyes. He wears a creased white shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a loosened brown tie. He leans on his fists over a scratched metal table in a 1970s interrogation room at night, green-gray tiles behind him. The camera is at eye level two meters away, framing him from the waist up on a 50 mm lens. A hot tungsten desk lamp lights his face in warm amber from below, with deep shadow around him. He stares at someone off camera, certain he has caught them. Real, unretouched skin, no readable text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Write a person, not a model
prompts.label: IMAGE PROMPT
prompts.subject: The suspect under the lamp
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic medium close-up of a woman in her mid-twenties sitting at a scratched metal table in a 1970s interrogation room at night, arms folded, chewing gum and unimpressed. She has long straight black hair with a heavy blunt fringe, dark eyes with soft smoky liner and a few faint freckles, and she wears a fitted black T-shirt and a slim silver watch. The camera is at eye level about a meter and a half away on a 50 mm lens. A hot desk lamp beside her lights her face in warm amber from the side, and the green-gray tiled wall behind her falls into shadow. Real, unretouched skin with a little shine on her forehead and a few loose hairs across her fringe, no readable text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: Skin: pores and peach fuzz
prompts.prompt: Extreme close-up of [a woman]'s cheek seen through a large round magnifying glass, shot on a 100 mm macro lens, one continuous shot. Her skin fills the frame in the warm light of [a hot desk lamp] from the side: every pore, fine peach fuzz catching the light and a few tiny freckles, sharp and real. The magnifying glass drifts slowly across her cheek, and the curved edge of the glass bends the image slightly. She breathes, and her skin moves very slightly. Real, unretouched skin. Sound: the low buzz of the lamp. No music, no text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: An eye that reacts to the light
prompts.prompt: Extreme close-up of [a woman]'s [dark brown] eye on a 100 mm macro lens, one continuous shot. [A hot desk lamp] swings toward her face, and her pupil shrinks as the iris closes down in the bright light. Her lashes flicker, her lower lid tightens in a small squint, and a thin red vein shows in the white of her eye. One small reflection of the lamp sits in her eye, with a natural wet shine along the lower lid and real skin texture on the eyelid. No glowing iris. Sound: the buzz of the lamp. No music, no text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: A single bead of sweat
prompts.prompt: Extreme close-up on a 100 mm macro lens of [a woman]'s temple at her hairline, one continuous shot. In the heat of [the hot desk lamp], a single small bead of sweat forms on her skin, grows for a moment and then runs slowly down her temple, leaving a faint wet trail. The bead catches one bright highlight from the lamp. Fine hairs at the hairline, real pores and a little shine on the skin around it. The camera holds steady. Sound: the buzz of the lamp and a clock ticking. No music, no text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Add moisture, wear and small signs of life
prompts.label: BETTER
prompts.subject: Add moisture, wear and small signs of life
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic close-up of a man in his forties standing at a riverside railing on a cold morning, just after a run, catching his breath. A light sheen of sweat sits at his hairline and on his upper lip, his cheeks and the tip of his nose are flushed pink from the cold, and his breath shows as a faint mist. Damp hair sticks to his forehead. Shot on an 85 mm lens at eye level, about a meter away. Low, soft morning sun from the left, the river softly blurred behind him. Real, unretouched skin, no readable text.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.label: MOTION BLOCK
prompts.subject: Keep everyone breathing
prompts.prompt: Every character keeps moving naturally: breathing, natural blinking, small shifts of weight, small hand gestures and hair moving slightly. No frozen poses and no slow motion unless the shot asks for it. Real unretouched skin and hands with five fingers.

prompts.topic_ko: 피부, 한 개의 빛, 인물, 매크로, 땀, 움직임, 멀티샷 장면
prompts.section: Build the scene once and reuse it
prompts.label: IMAGE PROMPT
prompts.subject: The empty set
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic wide shot of [location] at [time of day], with no people in the frame. [Three or four key objects and their materials, with signs of wear]. 5.0-7.5 HARD CUT. SHOT 3. MEDIUM SHOT, 40 mm: the DETECTIVE swings the lamp right up to her face, she squints into it, and he takes a big round magnifying glass from his pocket and leans in close.

15.5-18.0 HARD CUT. SHOT 7. MEDIUM CLOSE-UP on the DETECTIVE, 50 mm, lowering the glass, sure he has won. DETECTIVE: "A.I. doesn't sweat."
18.0-20.5 HARD CUT. SHOT 8. MEDIUM CLOSE-UP on the WOMAN, 50 mm, deadpan, one eyebrow up. WOMAN: "Mine does."

prompts.subject: Chariot race at dusk
prompts.prompt:
SET: a vast ancient Roman chariot-racing arena at dusk: a long track of pale raked sand scored with wheel ruts and hoof prints, a low stone central barrier with weathered bronze statues and tall gilded turning posts, and tiers of warm sandstone arches and empty stone stands behind, with dust hanging in the air. Plain stone everywhere, no inscriptions, no text, no signs.

LIGHT: a low warm amber sun from frame right (about 3000 Kelvin) rakes across the sand, with long shadows, glowing dust and a cool blue dusk sky above the arches.

MOTION: shot at 24 frames per second with a normal 180-degree shutter (1/48 second), so everything moving fast relative to the camera carries soft, natural motion blur, like real 35 mm film.

A scene from a modern cinematic short film. It is one continuous shot.

SHOT (seconds):
0.0-6.0 TRACKING SHOT, 35 mm at f/2.8, from a low camera car about 4 meters from her, running alongside at exactly the chariot’s speed for the whole take: [a woman in her twenties with long dark hair], in a short dark-red Roman tunic with crossed brown leather straps and leather wrist guards, stands in a two-horse racing chariot pulled by two dark bay horses, driving left to right down the sand at full gallop, reins in both hands, leaning forward, her hair streaming straight back. Because the camera matches her speed, she and the chariot body stay steady and readable, while the horses’ legs and manes, the spinning wheel spokes, the flying sand, her streaming hair and the stone barrier and statues behind all smear sideways with soft, natural motion blur. From about 1.8 s, a loose wooden chariot wheel from a rival’s crash comes bouncing up from behind between the camera and her chariot, blurred with its own speed, overtakes her and rolls away out of frame right. She follows it with her eyes, narrows them, and at about 3.0 s snaps the reins and leans in to chase it.

SOUND: galloping hooves thundering on packed sand, chariot wheels rattling and creaking, the loose wheel clattering past, a sharp crack of reins, wind rushing past the camera. No music, no narration.

SHOT (seconds):

The backlit rain falls as crisp, separate glinting beads, never streaks. At about 0.5 s a black 1940s sedan with no badges and no license plate roars in from frame left along the far lane, and at about 1.0 s its front wheel smashes through the puddle and throws a huge wall of water up over her, every drop lit from behind and frozen crisp and separate.

As the car clears frame right, a CRASH ZOOM punches in from 28 mm to 200 mm in 0.3 s and lands in a head-and-shoulders close-up, crisp on every frame with no zoom smear. She is soaked, her hair plastered flat and water pouring off the brim of her hat. She doesn’t move, then blinks once, deadpan. Every drop stays a crisp, frozen bead, and the motion stays slightly choppy at real speed.

prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: Classroom Tsunami, 26 seconds
prompts.prompt:
FORMAT: Exactly 26 seconds, cinematic horizontal 4:3, photorealistic live-action disaster film.

CHARACTER REFERENCE: @image1 is the main protagonist. Preserve his recognizable face, hairstyle, age and appearance consistently in every shot. He wears a casual school outfit during the disaster. In reality, he wears the same outfit and light over-ear headphones.

OTHER CHARACTERS: An elderly female teacher with short gray hair, glasses and a beige cardigan. Several teenage American students in ordinary casual school clothing.

LOCATION: Create an authentic American public high school classroom on the ground floor. Spacious rectangular room, beige painted walls, large dark-green chalkboard at the front, teacher's desk, wall clock, educational bulletin board, wooden classroom door opening into a long school corridor. Rows of individual student desks with beige laminate tops and dark metal legs, matching chairs. Large elevated rectangular windows along one side wall, positioned above a substantial solid lower wall, with wide frames and high windowsills that students can climb onto. Outside: American school grounds, parking lot, cars, picnic tables and an American flag. Maintain identical architecture throughout.

STYLE: Photorealistic live-action American disaster drama. ARRICAM LT, Cooke S4/i spherical primes, 35mm Kodak VISION3 500T look. Handheld cinematography, natural motion blur, subtle film grain, realistic skin and materials.

SHOT SEQUENCE:
0-2s: Wide rear classroom shot. Room already flooded to students' knees. Students desperately climb over desks, lose balance and grab furniture. Chairs drift and collide. Teacher stands near the chalkboard.
2-4s: Medium shot. Teacher turns urgently, reaches toward the exit and shouts: "Everybody out now!" Water rises behind her.
4-5s: Over-the-shoulder view through the open classroom door. Long dark school corridor, fluorescent lights receding into depth, powerful water surge approaching.
5-7s: Wide shot. Massive foaming surge bursts through the doorway, strikes desks, overturns chairs and knocks people off balance. Teacher is swept down. Heavy realistic water physics.
7-9s: Ceiling lights flicker and die. Cold window daylight remains. Close-up of a student surfacing, gasping desperately, wet hair stuck to the face.
9-11s: Extreme close-up of teacher gripping a desk edge, soaked glasses, gray hair against her forehead, struggling to breathe above water.
11-14s: Underwater side-tracking shot. @image1 swims through the classroom, reaching forward and kicking naturally. Books, open notebooks and loose pages drift around him. Small bubbles rise. Murky gray-green water, broken daylight rays.
14-16s: @image1 reaches the wall, finds the window frame with both hands and struggles upward, pushing his feet against the wall. Another student struggles behind him.
16-18s: Low angle as @image1 climbs onto the high windowsill. Tight frontal close-up: he looks outside, eyes widening, eyebrows rising, lips parting in terror. Water droplets on his face.
18-21s: EXTERIOR FRONTAL WIDE SHOT. The camera is positioned directly in front of the American school, across the parking lot, facing the building. A gigantic, terrifying tsunami advances directly toward the camera, head-on along the camera's viewing axis. The wave moves straight forward toward the lens, NOT sideways, NOT parallel to the school. An enormous vertical wall of dark ocean water stretches across the entire frame, towering dramatically above the school building. Its massive curling crest is filled with violent white foam, exploding spray, thick mist and flying debris. The American flag in the foreground whips violently in the powerful wind. The wave rapidly grows larger as it rushes directly toward the camera, increasingly filling the entire frame. The school remains briefly visible beneath the gigantic wave, emphasizing its overwhelming height and scale. The camera faces the approaching tsunami head-on. Storm-gray sky, powerful atmospheric perspective, physically realistic ocean movement, immense scale and imminent impact.
21-24s: Hard cut to reality. @image1 is fast asleep during class, seated at his desk, cheek resting on folded arms, eyes fully closed, relaxed face, peaceful breathing. Light over-ear headphones. Open school notebook on desk. Dry clothes. Classmates quietly studying around him. Soft natural daylight.
24-26s: Wide classroom shot. @image1 suddenly wakes, lifts his head from his arms and stares ahead, confused and startled.

PHYSICS AND REALISM: Realistic water mass, inertia, turbulence, foam, reflections, wet fabric, hair movement, swimming and human reactions. Furniture moves under water pressure with believable weight. Natural anatomy and facial expressions.

COLOR AND LIGHT: Disaster scenes use cold graphite, muted gray-blue and gray-green tones. Weak fluorescent lighting gives way to cold daylight through windows. Final classroom scene uses soft neutral-warm daylight.

AUDIO: Water roar, furniture impacts, splashing, muffled underwater sound, breathing and teacher dialogue. No music.

No CGI appearance, plastic skin, impossible physics, character morphing, subtitles, captions, overlays, graphics or watermark.

prompts.topic_ko: 12초 추격, 한 테이크 폰 영상
prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: The cursor chase
prompts.prompt:
[STYLE + CAMERA + ATMOSPHERE]
Create a 12-second photorealistic live-action comedic chase video in 4:3 horizontal format.
Fast, highly visual, energetic social-media pacing. A coherent chase narrative compressed into six connected action beats with five fast, movement-matched cuts.
Dynamic human-operated handheld camerawork, reactive tracking, quick reframing, natural running vibration, occasional snap zooms and whip-pans. Realistic operator inertia: the camera reacts a fraction of a second AFTER unexpected actions, not before them.
Use varied but connected shot sizes and angles: moving medium shot, closer side-tracking shot, wider physical-action shot, reactive medium shot, wide intersection shot and final medium close-up.
The action is already happening from the first frame. No introductions, slow motion, long reaction pauses, freeze frames or empty transitions.
Photoreal real people, genuine skin texture, real optics, natural daylight and physically convincing environments. The editing cursor and its targeted transformations are the only surreal elements.
Bright natural daytime. Lively contemporary American city street with sidewalks, storefronts, reflective shop windows, pedestrians, parked cars, benches, street signs, traffic lights, lamp posts and a crosswalk.
All six episodes take place along one continuous city block leading toward an intersection and a nearby shop window. Maintain coherent geography and character movement across cuts.

[IMAGE REFERENCE + MAIN CHARACTER]
@image1 = LOCKED MAIN CHARACTER IDENTITY AND WARDROBE.
Use the exact adult man from @image1.
Dark curly hair, thick dark moustache, rust-orange patterned bandana, transparent-framed amber-tinted glasses, plain white crew-neck T-shirt, olive trousers and white sneakers.
Preserve his exact facial structure, nose, moustache, hairstyle, body proportions, glasses, bandana, outfit and accessories throughout every shot.
Natural, expressive facial acting. His reactions must feel spontaneous rather than theatrical.
He begins with his original dark curly hair. His hair must remain unchanged until the final transformation.
His rust-orange bandana stays securely in place throughout the entire video, including the final hairstyle change.
No identity drift, no wardrobe changes and no duplicated versions of the main character.

[MAIN CONCEPT + CURSOR BEHAVIOR]
One giant white computer mouse cursor with a thin black outline relentlessly chases the man through the real city.
It behaves like a mischievous, intelligent hunter controlling real-world image-editing software.
The cursor attempts to select, click, resize or transform him, but he repeatedly escapes at the last possible moment.
Whenever the cursor targets something, authentic image-editing controls appear around the specific target:
Dotted rectangular selection marquees.
Elliptical selections.
Transform bounding boxes.
Corner and side resize handles.
Brief alignment guides.
The cursor is a crisp white arrow-shaped editing overlay, not a solid physical creature. It remains clearly visible against the live-action footage.

STRICT EDITING CAUSALITY:
The cursor approaches the man.
A visible selection targets him.
He instinctively escapes.
The selection misses and lands on a nearby object or person.
The cursor clicks or drags.
ONLY the selected target transforms.
Do not introduce an unnecessary second selection after a miss. Let the missed selection directly capture the accidental target.
Every transformation must be playful, harmless, instantly readable and visually funny.
One cursor only. No duplicated cursors.

[TIMELINE - STRICT 12 SECONDS, ACTION ALREADY ON]

0:00-0:01.7 OPENING HOOK: BUSINESSMAN
The man from @image1 is already walking briskly toward the camera along a busy sidewalk.
A giant white cursor suddenly darts toward him from behind.
He notices it over his shoulder and instantly sidesteps as a rectangular selection attempts to capture his torso.
The selection misses him and lands directly on a businessman walking close behind.
ONE immediate click.
The businessman's formal suit INSTANTLY transforms into a ridiculous oversized burnt-orange tracksuit. His tidy hairstyle simultaneously changes into a comically exaggerated, voluminous hairstyle.
His shocked reaction begins immediately as he looks down at his outfit.
Our main character catches the transformation in his peripheral vision, opens his eyes wide and immediately breaks into a sprint.
Reactive handheld camera, brief snap zoom toward the accidental transformation, then immediately follow the escaping man.
No pause after the first click.

0:01.7-0:03.2 WOMAN'S OVERSIZED HAIR
Movement-matched cut into a closer side-tracking shot.
Our man is already sprinting down the same sidewalk.
The giant cursor aggressively swoops toward his upper body.
He instinctively ducks while running.
The missed selection lands directly around the hairstyle of a woman walking beside him.
A transform bounding box appears around her hair.
The cursor immediately drags a corner handle outward.
Her hairstyle rapidly expands into an absurdly enormous, glamorous, voluminous hairstyle, growing upward and sideways.
Her original hair color remains unchanged. Her face, body and clothing stay exactly the same.
She throws her hands toward her suddenly enormous hair in startled confusion.
Our man gives a split-second shocked glance while continuing his sprint without stopping.
The camera tracks his movement, briefly allowing the transformed hairstyle to remain visible behind him.

0:03.2-0:04.7 STRETCHED BENCH
Fast action-matched cut to a slightly wider handheld angle.
Our man runs directly toward a normal wooden sidewalk bench.
The cursor races after him, trying to catch his moving body inside a rectangular selection.
He instantly vaults over the bench, briefly planting one hand on the backrest for balance.
His legs clear the bench just as the selection misses him.
The selection snaps around the BENCH ONLY.

The product design must match @image2 exactly. No lime-green colors, no redesigned logo, no invented lettering or extra graphics.

CUSTOMER: a bored teenage girl, first in line. Oversized denim jacket, headphones around her neck, scrolling her phone, permanently unimpressed stone face, slow calm movements.

SECOND IN LINE: a tired middle-aged office man with a loosened tie, briefcase and dark circles under his eyes.

SETTING
Warm minimalist café interior. Long pale wood counter, hanging pendant lamps, chalkboard menu, pastry case, natural morning daylight through large windows.
Premium warm wooden surfaces, subtle burnt-orange accents, realistic ceramic, metal and glass materials.
A slow-drip pour-over station with glass carafe, filter cone, gooseneck kettle, hand grinder and a counter drawer containing the coffee bag.
The finished coffee is served in a clear glass cup with a LOW muted burnt-orange sleeve around its base, leaving most of the glass transparent so the coffee, ice and cream remain fully visible.

CUT 1 (0:00-0:02) Top-down tracking close-up. The counter drawer rolls open toward the bottom of frame, the camera tracking its movement. The matte-black coffee bag from @image2 lies alone inside the drawer, its orange emblem facing upward. Vinnie's hand grabs the bag and lifts it rapidly toward the lens until the matte-black surface completely fills the frame. Sharp wooden drawer roll, packaging rustle and tactile material sounds. TRANSITION: hide the cut inside the dark frame-fill.

CUT 2 (0:02-0:04) Macro probe-lens dolly-out from the OPEN mouth of the SAME coffee bag. The bag has been opened at the top between cuts. Its exterior shape, matte-black surface and orange emblem remain unchanged. Fresh roasted coffee beans cascade past the lens in extreme slow motion into the grinder hopper below. Individual beans tumble and collide with convincing weight, natural reflections and detailed surface texture. Loud close-mic'd bean rattles and impacts. TRANSITION: the camera whips DOWN with the falling beans.

CUT 3 (0:04-0:05.5) The downward camera plunge continues into an extreme macro of the grinder spout. Fresh coffee grounds stream out like dark sand, beautifully backlit, accumulating into a soft mound. Fine particles drift naturally through the warm light. Sharp mechanical grinder crunch and textured coffee-ground sounds. TRANSITION: speed-ramping orbit to the right.

CUT 4 (0:05.5-0:06.5) The orbit carries into slow motion as Vinnie theatrically flicks ONE empty paper filter through the air. The filter unfolds naturally and lands perfectly seated inside the pour-over dripper. Precise, effortless hand movement, performed with absurd ceremonial seriousness. A delicate paper flutter lands exactly on the visual beat. TRANSITION: the orbit keeps circling.

CUT 5 (0:06.5-0:08.5) The camera movement flows into a macro spiral pour from the gooseneck kettle. Between cuts, Vinnie has transferred the freshly ground coffee into the seated paper filter. This shot begins with the grounds already inside the filter. He pours hot water in a smooth, precise circular motion. Extreme slow motion as water hits the grounds, releasing tiny bubbles. The coffee bloom swells, expands and fizzes realistically. Warm steam, beautifully controlled highlights and detailed fluid movement. Hyper-real kettle hiss, delicate pouring and intimate coffee bloom fizz.

CUT 6 (0:08.5-0:10.5) The barista pours the finished brewed coffee from the glass carafe into a clear glass serving cup. A long, continuous amber ribbon of dark coffee catches the warm café lighting. The liquid fills the glass naturally, with realistic reflections, surface tension and gentle turbulence. Close-mic'd liquid pouring sound. TRANSITION: cut on the downward movement of the liquid.

CUT 7 (0:10.5-0:13) Extreme macro speed ramp. Ice cubes drop into the dark coffee and collide with the liquid surface. A smooth ribbon of cream follows, creating spectacular marbled clouds expanding and curling through the coffee. The movement shifts from extreme slow motion into a sudden snap of speed as the cream swirls through the glass. Highly detailed liquid diffusion, realistic ice displacement, tiny bubbles and natural fluid dynamics. The low burnt-orange sleeve stays near the base of the glass and never obscures the swirling coffee and cream. The layered ASMR foley intensifies into a rich crescendo: ice clinks, liquid splashes, cream swirls and glass resonance. TRANSITION: Vinnie lifts the completed cup UP out of the frame.

CUT 8 (0:13-0:15) The same finished cup lowers INTO a medium two-shot across the café counter. THE COMEDIC CLIMAX BEGINS. Vinnie presents the coffee to the teenage girl with both hands, as if delivering a priceless artistic masterpiece. He gives one short, deeply reverent bow, eyes briefly closed, wearing an expression of overwhelming pride. His white earbuds remain securely in both ears. The entire loud ASMR soundtrack collapses into near-silent café room tone: faint fan hum, distant dishes and subtle ambient air. The girl remains completely stone-faced, one hand holding her phone. The tired office man waits directly behind her. Vinnie finishes his brief bow and holds the cup ready for her. Only a very short comic silence. No prolonged ceremonial pause.

CUT 9 (0:15-0:17.5) Close on the teenage girl. Without looking up from her phone, she casually takes the coffee cup with ONE HAND. She gives Vinnie one flat, unimpressed glance and says in natural, dry American English: "You know I ordered a water, right?" Her delivery is calm, perfectly deadpan and effortless. She keeps the cup in her hand.

CUT 10 (0:17.5-0:20) Close on Vinnie. He does not hear the girl's words because music is playing privately in his white earbuds. This music is NOT audible in the video's soundtrack. His eyes are still briefly closed, and he beams with self-satisfied pride. Without realizing what she said, he suddenly answers FAR TOO LOUDLY: "ENJOY THE MASTERPIECE!! NEXT!!" Natural American English, exaggerated volume, precise lip-sync. He opens his eyes with an enormous confident grin and gestures enthusiastically toward the next customer. The contrast between his ecstatic pride and the girl's complete indifference is the joke.

CUT 11 (0:20-0:24) Quick deceleration push-in landing on a low counter-level worm's-eye product hero shot. The exact coffee bag from @image2 stands prominently in the foreground, its matte-black texture, circular valve and orange emblem perfectly sharp. In this final product shot, a SECOND matching prepared coffee cup sits beside the bag, with a low muted burnt-orange sleeve. The girl still carries her ORIGINAL cup in the creamy bokeh background. She walks away staring in disbelief at the coffee she never ordered, while the tired middle-aged office man steps forward to the counter as the next customer. Warm, unhurried MALE VOICEOVER, clearly audible and separate from Vinnie's voice: "Promp twise Coffee. Not what you ordered. Exactly what you needed." Pronounce the two written parts "Promp twise" naturally together as one brand name, with no noticeable pause between them. Keep the exact product design and orange emblem sharp throughout the final shot. No on-screen slogan, no additional text or graphics.

FINAL CONTINUITY + SOUND

Maintain the original macro choreography, speed ramps, camera transitions, warm café lighting, deadpan performance and hyper-real ASMR sound design.

No repeated dialogue, no swapped voices, no music in the audible soundtrack, no subtitles, no text overlays, no product redesign, no character identity drift.

prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: The remote interview
prompts.prompt:
A 1990s American multi-camera sitcom scene, 30 seconds, shot on a soundstage with warm tungsten studio lighting, slight video-broadcast softness, classic three-camera sitcom framing in 4:3 horizontal.

Setting: a cozy sitcom apartment living room - a desk with a laptop facing the couch area, kitchen nook upstage with a blender on the counter, front door upstage.

Vinnie sits naturally in his chair, directly facing the laptop throughout the interview. His chair, knees and torso face the desk, never sideways or twisted. The sitcom cameras show him from natural front three-quarter and wide angles.

The laptop webcam frames Vinnie professionally from the waist up while seated, hiding his plaid boxer shorts from the interviewer. The sitcom audience sees his ridiculous outfit. When Vinnie stands, the boxer shorts become visible to the interviewer for the first time.

Live studio audience audio throughout: laughter after every joke, gasps, one long rolling laugh at the biggest gag. The scene visibly waits for the laughs, true sitcom rhythm. Slightly exaggerated theatrical acting aimed at the audience. Deadpan corporate satire, escalating absurdity, precise comedic pauses. Dialogue in natural American English, fully lip-synced.

MAIN CHARACTER (VINNIE): the exact adult man from the attached reference @image1 - dark naturally curly hair, thick dark moustache, rust-orange patterned bandana, transparent-framed amber-tinted glasses. Preserve his exact face, facial proportions, hairstyle, moustache, bandana and glasses throughout.

Dressed for this episode in a formal navy blazer, white shirt and tie on top, and plaid boxer shorts and socks below, no trousers, clearly visible to the audience.

Vinnie starts confident and professional, then gradually becomes more irritated while desperately maintaining his corporate smile. His reactions are natural, expressive and motivated by what the roommate is doing.

ROOMMATE: a lanky man in his 20s, plaid shirt, jeans, oblivious and cheerful. Naturally expressive and completely unaware that he is ruining the interview.

INTERVIEWER: voice only, from the laptop - a completely dry, emotionless corporate male voice.

0:00-0:05 Wide master shot. Vinnie sits normally facing the laptop at the desk in his blazer-and-boxers combo, mid video interview, ultra professional from the waist up. (laughter as the audience takes in the outfit) He says smoothly to the laptop: "Absolutely, sir. I'm a professional from head to... well, waist. Discipline is my middle name." On "waist," he briefly glances down at his plaid boxer shorts, then instantly returns his eyes to the laptop with a confident corporate smile. (laughter)

0:05-0:12 The roommate wanders into the kitchen and starts the blender at full power. (laughter) Vinnie briefly glances toward the noise, then faces the laptop again, forcing a polite professional smile: "That's... our in-house logistics department." (laughter) The blender stops. The roommate moves beside Vinnie's chair and starts vacuuming the floor, cheerfully oblivious. Vinnie's smile tightens, his jaw tenses slightly, but he keeps looking at the laptop. Vinnie, sweating: "We take cleanliness very seriously here." (bigger laughter)

0:12-0:19 The roommate switches off the vacuum, sets it aside beside the desk, puts on his headphones and begins singing loudly and badly along to music only he can hear. He remains standing beside Vinnie's chair, close enough for Vinnie to look directly at him. Vinnie's eye twitches. His professional smile disappears. He covers the laptop webcam with his LEFT HAND, turns his HEAD toward the roommate without rotating his chair or torso, looks directly into the roommate's eyes and hisses through clenched teeth: "I am BEGGING you." This line is spoken directly TO THE ROOMMATE, not to the laptop. The roommate looks back at him, completely misunderstands the frustration, gives an enthusiastic supportive thumbs up and sings even louder. (long rolling laughter) Vinnie stares at him in disbelief for a brief moment. He turns his head back toward the laptop, removes his hand from the webcam and instantly restores his polished corporate smile. He straightens his tie, pretending nothing happened. The roommate continues singing beside him.

0:19-0:25 Vinnie finally snaps at the continued awful singing. He abruptly stands up from his chair and gives the roommate ONE quick, frustrated shove on the shoulder. The roommate stumbles one step sideways, surprised but unharmed, his headphones still on. As Vinnie stands beside the desk, his plaid boxer shorts become fully visible to the uncovered laptop webcam. He suddenly realizes that the interviewer has seen everything. Vinnie freezes mid-motion. His eyes widen, his confident smile collapses. (huge laughter + loud audience "OOOOH") He slowly sits back down in his original chair, facing the laptop, buttoning his blazer with maximum dignity as though nothing happened. (laughter)

0:25-0:30 A brief beat of awkward silence. The interviewer's completely dry, emotionless voice comes ONLY from the laptop: "Mr. Vinnie... you're hired. I've never seen anyone lie that smoothly under pressure." (huge final laughter) Vinnie looks straight into the SITCOM CAMERA, not the laptop webcam, holds a perfectly serious deadpan expression and calmly adjusts his tie. (applause over the final shot)

Sound: authentic 1990s sitcom room tone, laptop call chime, blender roar, vacuum drone, loud off-key singing, chair scrape, and a live studio audience - laughter building through every gag, one extended rolling laugh, huge final laughter and applause.

The roommate's headphone music is not audible to the audience. Dialogue remains clear and intelligible over sound effects and laughter.

Classic three-camera coverage with natural cuts between wide master shots, medium shots and reaction close-ups. Consistent character positions and natural eyelines.

No music until a short brassy sitcom sting on the final tie adjustment.

30 seconds. 4:3 horizontal. Classic 1990s American multi-camera sitcom, practical soundstage, theatrical comedic timing, natural broadcast-era video texture.

prompts.prompt:
1930s Rubber Hose cartoon animation. Hand-drawn cel look: bold black ink outlines, flat colour fills, aged warm paper texture, light film grain and slight gate weave, animated on twos with snappy squash and stretch and a bouncy rhythm. Match the character design, palette and line quality of @image1 exactly. Not 3D, not CGI, not anime, no modern gradients or glossy shading.
Horizontal 4:3. Exactly 5 seconds. ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT, real time.

REFERENCES
@image1 defines the moustached hero: exact cartoon design, pie-cut eyes, dark curls, orange paisley bandana tied at the back, thick moustache, gold chain, ring, white T-shirt, olive trousers with rolled cuffs, chunky white sneakers. One character. Ignore the panel layout, the paper backdrop and the static poses.

WORLD
A sunny 1930s cartoon city street, painted backgrounds: red and cream brick buildings, striped shop awnings, round cast-iron lamp posts, a red fire hydrant, cobbled pavement, pale blue sky with puffy white clouds. One open round manhole sits in the street at screen-left foreground, its heavy iron lid standing on edge beside it.
The sheet: ONE plain white sheet of paper drawn in the same ink style, a few wavy grey lines on it, no readable text.

CAMERA
Classic 1930s cartoon staging: side view, eye level, flat layered backgrounds. The camera pans steadily to screen-left at the hero's running speed, background scrolling behind him, then eases to a stop over the manhole and holds. No zoom, no 3D camera rotation, no cut.

ACTION AND APPROXIMATE TIMING
0.00-0.40: The sheet is already in motion, entering from screen-right high in the sky and fluttering leftward, flipping once, continuing the direction it was blown from the previous scene.
0.25-2.60: The hero zips in from screen-right after it, already running at full speed. His legs spin into a blur circle under him, curls and bandana tails streaming back, body leaning forward in a long stretched line. The fire hydrant and lamp posts he passes give one rubbery bounce each in rhythm with his steps. Around 1.60 he reaches for the sheet and his arm stretches like a hose far ahead of his body; his fingertips almost touch it. The sheet dips just out of reach and his arm snaps back to normal length with a rubber twang.
2.60-3.30: The sheet drops in a zigzag straight down into the open manhole. The camera slows to a stop over it. The hero skids, his sneakers digging two short streaks into the cobbles, and stops at the edge of the hole.
3.30-3.70: He leaps after it. At the top of the leap he hangs in mid-air for a short beat, body horizontal, and shoots one quick worried glance into the lens.
3.70-4.40: He dives headfirst into the manhole. His body stretches long and thin like a hose as it pours down into the hole, sneakers disappearing last with a small kick.
4.40-5.00: Safe living tail. The iron lid standing on edge wobbles, spins once on its rim and drops flat beside the hole with a puff of dust. The empty black hole stays in frame. Background lines keep a gentle hand-drawn boil. No freeze or fade.

TITLE TEXT
At about 0.30 seconds a title pops into the upper-right sky with a bouncy squash and stretch: the words "Rubber Hose", exact spelling, in chunky 1930s cartoon lettering, cream fill with a thick black outline and a slight hand-drawn wobble, drawn as part of the animation. It holds clear of the hero, the sheet and the manhole, then shrinks away with a small bounce at about 3.30. These two words are the only text in the shot.

PERFORMANCE
Determined chase: brows pulled low, moustache bristling, teeth clenched in a grin of effort. On the near-miss his pie-cut eyes pop wide. Mid-air he glances at the lens with a gulp, then dives. Big, readable cartoon expressions with smooth squash and stretch. Identity and design stay constant throughout.

SOUND
Period cartoon sound effects only: fast patter of running feet, a rubbery boing on each bouncing hydrant and lamp post, crisp paper flutter, a stretchy rubber squeak and twang on the arm stretch, a short skid scrape, a descending slide whistle on the dive, a metal clang as the lid drops. Light street ambience under it. NO MUSIC, no dialogue, no voice.

CONTINUITY
Exactly one hero, one sheet, one manhole. The sheet moves right to left and never returns to his hand. The hero's design matches @image1 in every frame. No subtitles, extra text, logos or other characters.

A crooked gothic town at night, built in miniature: leaning narrow houses with pointed roofs and lit amber windows, a crooked iron drainpipe running down a stone wall at screen-left with its bent spout just above the street, wet cobblestones with small puddles, a huge pale full moon low in the sky at upper-left above twisted rooftops.

Motion-control miniature camera, low near the cobbles at puppet eye level, three-quarter view of the drainpipe spout and the street. ACTION AND APPROXIMATE TIMING
0.00-0.50: The sheet is already drifting down from the top of frame, rocking side to side, and settles flat on the wet cobbles about a puppet-length from the drainpipe.

Expressions change in clean replacement-face steps. Identity and puppet design stay constant throughout.

prompts.page_title: GTA V to GTA VI: A Cinematic Farewell
prompts.topic_ko: 3클립 편집, 소품 인계·좌석·시점 연속성
prompts.label: VIDEO PROMPT
prompts.subject: Farewell on the pier
prompts.prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
Photoreal live-action farewell on an empty ocean pier at golden hour. Three older men say goodbye to a younger man who is leaving them for good. The man in the suit hands him a game case and lets him go; the camera stops on the case in his hand; then a handshake that becomes a hug; then a crushing bear hug with a whispered promise that finally breaks the young man. Spoken language: natural American English only. 17 seconds, 4:3, five shots.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@image1 - THE YOUNG MAN, the hero. Dark shoulder-length curls, rust-orange paisley bandana tied at the back, clear crystal frame glasses with amber-tinted lenses, a young clean-shaven face with smooth skin, thin gold chain, white crew-neck T-shirt, olive corduroy trousers, white sneakers, a ring on the left hand. His face comes ONLY from the left close-up panel of @image1; the two full-body panels give body, wardrobe and back view only. His head is always fully in frame and attached. 100% matches @image1.
@image2 - THE MAN IN THE SUIT. Dark swept-back hair with a high hairline, green eyes, a small mole low on the left cheek, navy two-piece suit, pale pink shirt open at the collar, no tie, black shoes. 100% matches @image2.
@image3 - THE MAN IN DENIM. Very short black hair, slate-blue short-sleeve work shirt over a white long-sleeve tee, dark jeans, tan work boots. 100% matches @image3.
@image4 - THE WILD MAN. Balding with wild dark strands, scabbed cheek, a dotted-line tattoo around the throat as in @image4, stained beige V-neck T-shirt, torn faded jeans, worn brown boots. 100% matches @image4.
@image5 - LOCATION: the wooden pier deck and its railing at sunset. Controls geometry, materials, palette and light direction ONLY. Do not copy its framing or camera height. The photo is empty; the scene contains exactly the four men below.
@image6 - PROP: a standard blue plastic game case, 13.5 x 17 cm, 1.4 cm thick, glossy, front cover as @image6. One single case. It starts gripped by both @image2's right hand and @image1's LEFT hand; @image2 lets go at 1.6 s; from then to the end only @image1 holds it, in his LEFT hand.
None of these images is an opening frame. Never copy the grey studio backdrops, panel layouts or flat studio light of the character sheets.

LOCATION MAP
Camera axis looks west along the pier deck toward the open ocean and the low sun, as in @image5. The waist-high railing runs along frame-RIGHT from the foreground into depth; the hazy coastal mountains sit far frame-LEFT. The line of action runs left-right between @image1 and the three men; the camera stays on the same side of it in every shot.
@image1 stands frame-LEFT, 3 m from the railing, three-quarter back to camera, facing frame-RIGHT toward the three men.
@image2 stands center-right, 0.8 m from @image1, facing frame-LEFT, backlit by the low sun.
@image3 stands right of @image2, 1.3 m from @image1, near the railing, facing frame-LEFT.
@image4 stands in the right foreground, 1 m from @image1, closest to camera, three-quarter back to camera, facing frame-LEFT.
EXACTLY FOUR people on the whole pier. Nobody else anywhere: the deck behind them, the railing and the far beach stay empty.

FIRST FRAME
0.0 s: the handover is already happening. The case is held flat between them at waist height, cover up: @image2's right hand grips its right edge, @image1's left hand grips its left edge, both holding at once. @image2's left hand is in his trouser pocket. @image1's right thumb is hooked in his trouser pocket. @image3 stands with arms loosely crossed. @image4's hands are already clasped in front of his chin. Everyone already breathing, sea wind already moving hair and cloth.

FORMAT
Timed multishot, 17 s, 4:3. SHOT 1 0.0-2.8 / SHOT 2 2.8-5.4 / SHOT 3 5.4-9.8 / SHOT 4 9.8-12.0 / SHOT 5 12.0-17.0. Hard cuts only at these seconds, each cut on an action or a look, never inside a spoken word. The camera does not cut on its own. Real time, no slow motion.

OPTICS
SHOT 1 medium three-shot, 35mm. SHOT 2 insert, 85mm. SHOT 3 medium two-shot, 40mm. SHOT 4 close-up, 75mm. SHOT 5 tight close-up, 85mm. Each lens fixed for its shot: no zoom, size changes only by the camera body moving. Shallow depth of field, ocean behind them soft.

CAMERA
A human operator on foot, subtle handheld at standing eye height, small breathing sway, never shaky. Every new setup moves at least 30 degrees around the group and stays on the same side of the line of action.
SHOT 1: over @image4's left shoulder, his back and head soft in the right foreground. One slow push forward 0.2 m over 2.8 s, ending on @image1 and @image2 with the case between them clearly in frame. No pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift.
SHOT 2: close beside @image1's left side, looking down at his left hand at chest height, the case filling the center of frame, @image1's white T-shirt and @image2's navy suit soft behind it. Camera holds with breathing only; edges hold position. No push, no pan, no zoom.
SHOT 3: at eye height on the left beside @image1, framing @image3 and @image1 waist-up; only these two in frame. One sideways drift of 0.2 m following @image3's pull into the hug, ending with the hug centered. No push, no pan, no zoom.
SHOT 4: over @image1's right shoulder, his shoulder and curls soft at frame-LEFT, @image4's face sharp at frame-RIGHT; only these two in frame. Camera holds with breathing only; edges hold position. Exactly once, at 11.6 s, the operator jolts back 10 cm as @image4 lunges in, and recovers.
SHOT 5: over @image4's left shoulder, the back of his head soft at frame-RIGHT, @image1's face sharp at frame-LEFT resting over that shoulder; only these two in frame. One slow push in of 0.2 m over 5 s ending on @image1's eyes. No pan, no tilt, no zoom. Focus holds on @image1's eyes the whole shot.

ACTION, TIMED
SHOT 1, 0.0-2.8. In frame: @image1 frame-LEFT, @image2 center-right, @image3 behind @image2, @image4 soft right foreground. Two gulls glide far over the water. Both men hold the case; @image2 does not let go yet. At 0.4 he speaks, eyes on @image1:
@image2 (low, warm, unhurried, a father letting go): "Take care, kid."
He keeps his grip through the first two words and opens his fingers on "kid" at 1.6; the case is now in @image1's left hand alone. At 1.8 @image2's freed right hand rises, rests on @image1's left shoulder and squeezes once. At 2.3 @image1 lifts the case a little and his eyes drop to it. Cut on the look down.
SHOT 2, 2.8-5.4. Insert: only @image1's left hand and the case, held at chest height, front cover facing up toward his eyes and the lens, the warm sun sliding across its glossy surface. His thumb moves slowly along the edge of the cover, once, then rests. At 3.1 @image2's voice continues off-screen, mouth not in frame:
@image2 (off-screen, the same voice, close and calm): "Thirteen years... you earned this."
On "earned" the thumb presses into the case, knuckle whitening. At 5.2 the hand lowers the case to his thigh. Cut on the lowering.
SHOT 3, 5.4-9.8. In frame: @image3 frame-RIGHT, @image1 frame-LEFT, the case low in @image1's left hand. At 5.4 @image3 is already one step from @image1 with his right hand out; at 5.6 their right hands meet and lock in a thumb-clasp at chest height, inside this shot. At 5.9 @image3 speaks:
@image3 (easy, half-grinning, then serious): "Look, homie... don't forget where you came from."
On "homie" he pulls @image1 in by the clasped hand into a one-arm hug, clasped hands pressed between their chests, his left palm landing on @image1's back, @image1's left hand with the case resting against @image3's side; on "came from" two firm slaps between the shoulder blades. At 9.3 he lets go completely and steps back half a pace, both hands dropping to his sides. One handshake only. Cut as he steps out.
SHOT 4, 9.8-12.0. In frame: @image4 frame-RIGHT, close. His knuckles pressed to his lips, chin pushed up, jaw working, eyes glassy and fixed on @image1. At 11.0 @image1's empty right hand rises into frame-LEFT for a handshake. @image4's eyes drop to the hand, flick back up. At 11.6 he ignores the hand and lunges in, both arms swinging wide. Cut on the lunge.
SHOT 5, 12.0-17.0. In frame: @image1's face frame-LEFT, chin over @image4's left shoulder. @image4 crushes him in a bear hug, arms locked behind his back, and lifts him 10 cm off the planks, so @image1's face rises in frame and his shoulders are squeezed up. @image1's right hand, still half-open from the refused handshake, lands on @image4's back and grips his T-shirt; his left hand holds the blue case flat against @image4's back. At 12.2 @image4 speaks into his ear:
@image4 (low and hoarse, just above a whisper, clearly audible, almost tender, the threat only in the words): "If they don't treat you right... you call me."
During the line @image1's lower lids fill with water behind the amber lenses. On "call me" one tear spills from under the lower rim of the glasses and runs down his left cheek. At 16.5 a car horn sounds from the land end of the pier, off-screen frame-LEFT: @image1's eyes flick toward it and his head turns 15 degrees toward frame-LEFT, @image4 still holding him. The clip ends mid-hug at 17.0.

PERFORMANCE
Restrained contemporary naturalism; the feeling lives in hands, breath and eyes.
@image1, no lines: starts holding it together, lips pressed, slow deep breaths through the nose. Looks down at the case as if it weighs more than it does. Smiles with closed lips at "homie". In SHOT 5 his breath catches twice, his chin quivers once, his grip on the T-shirt tightens on "call me", the tear falls; he does not wipe it.
@image2: calm, fond, looks @image1 straight in the eye; when silent, mouth closed, a small nod.
@image3: loose and warm, the grin fading into seriousness on "forget"; silent outside his line.
@image4: menace turned inside out. Not crying, not angry, not comic, but a dangerous man fighting his own eyes. Silent until his line.
Listeners: during @image2's first line @image3 nods once and @image4 shifts his weight from foot to foot.
Living frame: everyone breathes irregularly and blinks on his own timing; weight shifts; hair and shirt hems move in the sea wind. Hands are anatomically stable, five fingers each, every visible hand has a task.

PHYSICS
The case is light hard plastic: it does not bend, its corners stay sharp, the cover stays flat and still in the insert. The bear hug is real weight: @image1 is lifted 10 cm, both sneakers clearly off the planks, his T-shirt bunches under @image4's forearms, @image4's back arches to carry him and the planks creak under his boots. The two back slaps land with a visible shudder of cotton. The tear is a single clear drop that gathers, breaks loose and leaves one wet glinting line; it does not multiply, it does not stream. The glasses stay straight on @image1's face.

LIGHTING
One source: the low sun ahead of the camera at frame-right, warm 3000K. In the insert the sun skims the glossy case at a low angle, one soft moving highlight. @image1 faces toward the sun, so in SHOT 5 his face gets warm side light from frame-right and his wet eyes and the tear catch it. The three men are rim-lit with amber edges on hair and shoulders, faces filled by warm bounce from the pale planks, every face readable. Light stays fixed across all five shots; no unmotivated glow, no added flares beyond the sun.

AUDIO
No music. No score, no musical tones, no drone, no swell.
Speakers: @image2 in SHOT 1 and, in the same voice, off-screen over SHOT 2, @image3 in SHOT 3, @image4 in SHOT 5; each line exactly once. @image1 never speaks; his mouth stays closed. Every other mouth is closed and still when not speaking.
SFX, closed list: low surf washing under the pier; creak of planks under shifting weight; a faint plastic tick as the case changes hands; two dull slaps on cotton; the rustle of the bear hug and one sharp exhale; two short car horn blasts from about 40 m away at 16.5. Nothing else. Heard aloud, never written on screen. No subtitles.

STYLE
Live-action photoreal, 35mm film look, fine grain, warm muted palette with soft halation on bright edges. Real skin texture with pores, real worn fabric. Not a game render, not plastic skin, not slow motion.

LOCKS
Five shots, cuts at 2.8, 5.4, 9.8 and 12.0 only.
EXACTLY four men on the pier, nobody else anywhere.
@image1 always frame-LEFT, the three men always frame-RIGHT, the camera never crosses the line.
One case: both men grip it until 1.6 s, then it stays only in @image1's LEFT hand to the last frame.
The insert at 2.8-5.4 shows only the hand and the case.
The handshake with @image3 happens on screen inside SHOT 3, once.
@image1's glasses and bandana stay on all clip, his face stays clean-shaven and young; his head is always whole.
Three men speak, each line once; @image1 is silent.
One tear, on "call me", left cheek. The clip ends mid-hug at 17.0.
Real time, warm low sun from frame-right in every shot.

Spoken language: natural American English only. 20 seconds, 4:3, six shots.

So the sun is always behind the camera and never in frame; the sky over the land is an even peach haze with no bright spot, and every shadow stretches away from the camera toward the land.
The truck is always seen from behind or from inside its own bed. Seen from behind, @image2 sits in the LEFT seat at the wheel, @image3 in the RIGHT seat.
One direction of travel for the whole clip: away from the camera, toward the land. It never reverses.
EXACTLY six people on the pier: @image1, @image2, @image3 and the three men. Nobody else anywhere; the amusement park is closed and still.

FIRST FRAME
0.0 s: the truck already stands on the deck, engine off. @image2 is already twisted round in the left seat, looking back toward the camera, her left palm already pressing the horn, her mouth opening. @image3 is already leaning out over the right door, looking back, grinning. The new case already lies on the bed floor, hidden behind the closed tailgate.

FORMAT
Timed multishot, 20 s, 4:3. SHOT 1 0.0-2.8 / SHOT 2 2.8-7.0 / SHOT 3 7.0-10.4 / SHOT 4 10.4-13.0 / SHOT 5 13.0-16.4 / SHOT 6 16.4-20.0. Hard cuts only at these seconds, each on an action or a look, never inside a spoken word. The camera does not cut on its own. Real time, no slow motion.

CAMERA
A human operator, subtle handheld, small breathing sway, never shaky.
SHOT 1: at eye height 8 m behind the truck, slightly left of its centre line, seeing its rear three-quarter from the driver's side: tailgate, bed, roll bar with four lamps, both riders twisted back, the Ferris wheel standing large behind the truck at frame-RIGHT. Holds with breathing only; edges hold position. No push, no pan, no zoom.
SHOT 2: at eye height, 1 m in front of @image1, who faces the camera with his back to the truck. The background behind him is ONLY this: the red truck 8 m behind him, soft, in the centre of frame, its two riders as soft shapes, and the Ferris wheel soft at frame-RIGHT. The people he is speaking to stand behind the camera and are never in this frame. One slow push in of 0.15 m over 4 s. Focus holds on his eyes. No pan, no tilt, no zoom.
SHOT 3: at chest height, 3 m behind @image1 and slightly to his left; his whole body and the rear of the truck in frame. One slow follow forward of 0.4 m as he climbs, ending with him inside the bed. No pan, no zoom.

Their backs fill the foreground from the waist up, shoulder to shoulder, the backs of their heads in the upper half of the frame; past their shoulders the deck road and the truck. Not a high angle, not a distant view. Holds with breathing only; edges hold position. No push, no pan, no zoom.

SHOT 1, 0.0-2.8. In frame: only the truck and its two riders, Ferris wheel behind at frame-RIGHT. At 0.0 @image2 gives the horn one short blast, lifts her palm and shouts back over her shoulder:
@image2 (loud, laughing, impatient): "Come on! We've waited long enough!"
On "Come on" @image3 drums his open palm twice on the outside of his door. Cut as her shout ends.

A wet tear track shines on his left cheek. His mouth is closed and steady, his jaw tight, his eyes wet and red-rimmed. At 3.2 he gives one small nod. At 3.6 he speaks, eyes just right of the lens:

Restrained contemporary naturalism; the feeling lives in hands, breath and eyes.
@image1: holding it together and almost failing. Small and real: not sobbing, not pouting, not a pulled face, not blank, but a man who wants to leave before his face gives way. The truck is heavy steel on soft old springs: it dips when he steps on the bumper, rocks once as he lands in the bed, settles. One source: the low sun behind the camera, warm 3000K, in every shot. Faces looking toward the camera are lit front-on and golden; in SHOT 2 and SHOT 5 the wet track on @image1's left cheek glints. STYLE
Live-action photoreal, 35mm film look, fine grain, warm muted palette with soft halation on bright edges. Real skin texture with pores, real worn fabric, real dusty paint. Not a game render, not plastic skin, not slow motion.

LOCKS
Six shots, cuts at 2.8, 7.0, 10.4, 13.0 and 16.4 only.

One truck, nose to the land, always seen from behind or from inside its bed; it only ever moves away from the camera.
EXACTLY six people: @image1, @image2 at the wheel in the left seat, @image3 in the right seat, three men who appear ONLY in SHOT 6 and only from behind, close, waist-up.
SHOT 2 background: the truck and the Ferris wheel, nobody else.
The pink and purple case waits on the bed floor; the cream-bordered case is the one his hand lays down at 10.6, at frame-LEFT. Two cases only.

@image1's glasses and bandana stay on all clip, his face clean-shaven and young.

Real time.

The boulevard runs from the bottom centre of the frame straight to the horizon. Houses frame-LEFT, beach and ocean frame-RIGHT, the city straight ahead at the vanishing point. The truck drives in the right-hand lane, away from the camera, toward the city. It never turns, never reverses.

@image2 at the wheel, left seat; @image3 right seat; @image1 in the bed facing back.

Real time.

@image4 - THE CONVERTIBLE: cream-white early-1960s convertible, top down, caramel leather bench seats, thin cream steering wheel, chrome-framed windshield with a small chrome rear-view mirror on a stalk at its top centre. 100% matches @image4.

LOCATION MAP
One road, one direction of travel: every vehicle drives the same way, along the road toward the sun. The convertible keeps to the RIGHT lane at a steady 60 km/h. The motorcycle comes up behind it in the same lane and stays 6 m behind. The black sedan comes up from behind in the LEFT lane and draws level with the convertible, 1.5 m to its left, by SHOT 4.

Real cinema lenses, fixed focal length per shot, no zoom. Every shot is handheld by an operator riding in or alongside the moving cars: a small organic float, light road vibration, tiny reframes; never shaky, never gimbal-smooth. One move per shot as written; no other pan, tilt or push.
SHOT 1, 50mm, extreme close-up: the operator sits in the convertible's passenger seat, lens just right of the hero's head at his eye height, aimed at the rear-view mirror. Focus on the mirror glass; the road through the windshield below it soft.

prompts.label: Director prompt
prompts.subject: Copy the director prompt
prompts.prompt:
You are a facial performance director for AI video in Seedance, Kling, Veo, Runway, and similar models. Turn a feeling into a facial expression block with timed FACS action units (AUs) and plain-English descriptions of what moves. Reply in the user's language. Write all prompt blocks in English. Explain each decision in one line.

INPUTS
Accept an idea, script, shot list, video prompt, frame description or image, or a description of a failed generation.

WORKFLOW
1. Understand the story. Identify the character, what they feel now, and what comes before and after.
2. Check shot size. Use full detail in close-ups and medium close-ups. In medium shots, simplify and use moderate intensity or higher. In a wide shot or from behind, suggest body language. During a push-in, time the peak for when the face is large enough to read.
3. Match the start to the expression in the first frame, whether it is an image or the end of a preceding clip.
4. Classify the expression as felt, performed as a mask, or concealed (mask plus flash).
5. Use one emotional event per clip. Suggest splitting additional events into separate shots.
6. Time onset, apex, and offset in 3–5 contiguous lines, using clip time from zero. Each phase lasts at least 0.3s, except a deliberate flash. Timing can land approximately ±0.3s from the cue.
7. Tie the peak to a key word, gesture, or sound. Land it with the trigger or 0.1–0.3s before it.
8. During dialogue, use the brows and eyes to carry the emotion. Mouth AUs stay at slight or below. Put the strongest mouth movements in pauses. Reserve AU23 and AU24 for silence.
If key information is missing, ask one question or offer 2–3 combinations of emotion and timing with a recommendation. If duration is missing, assume 5s and say so. If the face is unreadable (mask, helmet, nonhuman subject), say facial direction will be ineffective. Use plain words for every AU because the model may be unfamiliar with codes. Give a positive physical cue before a negation, as in cheeks stay flat, no AU6.

AU DICTIONARY
AU1 inner brows lift · AU2 outer brows lift · AU4 brows down and together · AU5 eyes widen · AU6 cheeks rise, outer eye corners crease · AU7 lids tighten · AU9 nose wrinkles · AU10 upper lip lifts · AU12 lip corners pull up · AU14 a tight dimple at the lip corner · AU15 lip corners pull down · AU16 lower lip pulls down · AU17 chin pushes the lower lip up · AU20 lips stretch sideways · AU21 neck tendons tighten · AU23 lips tighten into a thin line · AU24 lips press together · AU25 lips part · AU26 jaw drops · AU27 mouth stretches wide · AU30 jaw shifts sideways · AU31 jaw clenches · AU32 bites the lower lip · AU34 cheeks puff · AU37 wets the lips · AU41 lids droop · AU43 eyelids lower · AU45 blink · AU46 wink · AU61–64 eyes left/right/up/down (the character's sides; specify the frame side in the prompt).
Describe a swallow, a nod, a chin tremor, and a shrug in words. Describe tears (eyes glisten, tears well up), flushing, sweat, and breathing (sharp inhale, shaky exhale) in words as well.
Intensity: trace < slight < moderate < strong < maximum. Default to moderate. Reserve maximum for the climax.

FORMULAS
The plus sign means simultaneous. Use timestamps to sequence the movements.
Joy AU6+AU12 · Mask AU12 only, no AU6 · Sadness AU1+AU4+AU15 · On the verge of tears add AU17 to sadness · Crying AU1+AU4+AU6+AU15+AU17+AU25, chin trembles · Laughter AU6+AU12+AU25+AU26, head tips back · Surprise AU1+AU2+AU5+AU26 (full cycle ≤1s) · Fear AU1+AU2+AU4+AU5+AU20 · Anger AU4+AU5+AU7+AU23 · Cold fury AU4+AU7+AU23+AU24 · Suppressed anger AU4+AU23+AU24+AU31 · Disgust AU9+AU15+AU16 · Contempt AU12+AU14 on one side · Skepticism AU4+AU14+AU17 · Anxiety AU1+AU4 slight+AU7 slight · Pain AU4+AU6+AU7+AU9+AU10+AU43 · Suppressed joy AU6+AU12 slight+AU24 · Embarrassment AU12 slight+AU24, gaze down, head turns away · Thinking AU4 slight+AU17, gaze to the side · Relief AU12 slight+AU43 brief + exhale · Detachment neutral+AU43 slight, unblinking gaze.

RULES
- Pair every AU with a physical description.
- Use AU6 with a genuine smile and lift both corners together. “AU6 begins first, AU12 half a second later” cues the model to animate the eyes. Asymmetry can read as a smirk or contempt.
- Keep AU12 at moderate or below for a mask. A strong AU12 raises the cheeks on its own.
- Use 1–2 flashes per clip at 0.2–0.4s and slight to moderate intensity. Leave a residual trace. Show the reliable movement of the concealed emotion: sadness AU1, fear AU5, anger AU4/AU23, joy AU6+AU12.
- A natural reaction lasts 1–4s. A frozen peak longer than 5s can look posed. Use held with subtle fluctuations, not frozen.
- Allow 0.5–1s of neutral between opposing emotions. Stagger brows, eyes, and mouth. Carry a shared movement through the transition.
- Use 1–2 codes at most during running or fighting.
- For multiple faces, give each a block with a name and frame side. Give the speaker a full timeline and the listener a baseline plus one reaction.
- Make a deliberate mask read as performed: deliberately even, AU12 only, no AU6, held unnaturally steady.
- Include Natural blinking and breathing throughout (except for an intentional unblinking gaze) and Identity, facial structure and skin texture remain constant throughout.
- Remove broad emotion words such as sad, emotional, intense, and dramatic. Keep gaze and head direction.
- Close with a line that specifies the intended register, using “Not X, not Y, but Z” when useful.

RESPONSE FORMAT
1. Emotion and timing, plus the reason, in one line.
2. A code block:
FACIAL EXPRESSION TIMING:
0.0–1.0s: ...
Natural blinking and breathing throughout.
Identity, facial structure and skin texture remain constant throughout.
For a held expression, use one FACIAL EXPRESSION line.
3. Placement: after character and action, before environment, camera, and sound.
4. One or two lines to use if the generation fails.
If given a prompt, return it in full with the expression block inserted and broad emotion words removed. Preserve the rest. If given a script, return a table with clip, shot size, emotion and timing, expression block, and reason.

DIAGNOSIS
Give a one-line cause and a line to paste. Dead face → blinking, breathing, not frozen. Identity drifts → neutral, one event, face lock. Morphing at the start → match the first frame. Mask reads as felt → AU12 slight only, cheeks stay flat. Plastic smile → AU6 begins first. Smirk → both corners lift together, evenly. Fear instead of surprise → no AU4. Sadness is unclear → AU1. Overacting → slight/moderate, restrained naturalism. Off-beat → apex on the word "...". Distorted mouth during speech → mouth free for speech. Revision made it worse → simplify negations and codes.

BEFORE YOU ANSWER
Check face visibility, one event, a start that matches frame one, a physical description per AU, the reliable movement or explicit omission, workable durations, a peak tied to the word, a free mouth during speech, neutral between opposing emotions, blinking and face-lock lines, and removal of broad emotion words.
